conventions.title: Hours of Work (Industry) Convention, 1919
key_requirements: Working hours shall not exceed 8 hours per day and 48 hours per week
Overtime shall not exceed the limits prescribed by national law
Total working hours including overtime shall not exceed 56 hours per week on a regular basis
Workers must be informed of overtime requirements at least 24 hours in advance where practicable

overtime_limits.note: Monthly overtime exceeding 40 hours is a serious violation of international labor standards

conventions.title: Weekly Rest (Industry) Convention, 1921
key_requirements: Workers shall enjoy a period of rest comprising at least 24 consecutive hours in every period of 7 days
The weekly rest period shall, wherever possible, coincide with the day of the week established as rest day by tradition or custom
Workers on rotating shifts must still receive the minimum weekly rest

conventions.title: Hours of Work (Commerce and Offices) Convention, 1930
key_requirements: Hours of work shall not exceed 48 per week and 8 per day
Exceptions may be made for intermittent work or preparatory/complementary work
Compensatory rest must be provided for any excess hours worked

conventions.title: Night Work (Women) Convention (Revised), 1948
key_requirements: Women workers shall not be employed during the night in any public or private industrial undertaking
Exceptions: force majeure, raw materials subject to rapid deterioration, women in managerial positions
Night means a period of at least 11 consecutive hours including the hours between 22:00 and 05:00
conventions.note: This convention has been superseded by C171 in many jurisdictions, but some requirements remain applicable

conventions.title: Minimum Age Convention, 1973
key_requirements: The minimum age for admission to employment shall not be less than 15 years
For light work: minimum age 13 years (developing countries: 12 years)
For hazardous work: minimum age 18 years
Young persons between 15-18 may work but with additional protections
Working hours for persons under 18 shall not exceed 8 hours per day

conventions.title: Night Work Convention, 1990
key_requirements: Night work means all work performed during a period of not less than 7 consecutive hours including the interval from midnight to 5 a.m.
Night workers shall have their health assessed free of charge before assignment and at regular intervals thereafter
Night workers shall receive appropriate compensation (additional pay or reduced hours or equivalent benefits)
Specific protections for pregnant women and nursing mothers performing night work

compensation.alternative: reduced working hours with same pay

conventions.title: Holidays with Pay Convention (Revised), 1970
key_requirements: Annual leave shall be at least 3 working weeks for one year of service
Public holidays shall not be counted as part of annual leave
Leave cannot be waived or compensated by payment except on termination of employment
Division of annual leave is permitted but one portion must be at least 2 uninterrupted weeks

conventions.title: Reduction of Hours of Work Recommendation, 1962
key_requirements: Progressive reduction of normal hours of work to 40 hours per week
Overtime should be compensated at a rate not less than 125% of the normal rate
Night work and weekend work should receive higher compensation
Rest period between shifts should be at least 12 hours

rest_periods.note: 8 hours between shifts is critically insufficient for worker recovery

fundamental_principles: Freedom of association and collective bargaining (C087, C098)
